Theme

gravel noun

classical

Livy 41.27.5 (Lewis & Short)
M-O s.v. gravel
Cato, Agr. 18.7: dē glāreā et calce harēnātō prīmum corium facitō, the first layer of a floor
Vitruvius 2.4.2: sand sifted ē glāreā
Cicero, Q. fr. 3.1.4: pulvis, nōn glārea injecta est, of an approach road on a slope

glārea, glāreae f.

noun, first declension · Declension on Wiktionary

A collective material noun. Lewis & Short cites road-building use. Morgan–Owens also lists it.

Other words

  • calculus — gravel in the medical sense

    noun, second declension · avoid · classical · Declension on Wiktionary

    The medical “gravel” sense of calculus at the same Morgan–Owens headword is not the building material intended here.

Examples

  • Glāream hūc fer.

    Bring the gravel here.composed

  • Hīc glāream cumulā.

    Pile the gravel here.composed

See also sand, stone, pile up, mortar, ground.

SourcesLewis & Short: glarea · Morgan–Owens: gravel
